chunks: What Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning

A well into which a child urinates, or urine is poured into it, or wine is poured into it—he said: all of the water is to be drawn out. So what this report includes of mentioning urine together with wine is to be understood as when one of the qualities of the water has changed, because if it has not changed, then it has a specific fixed amount to be drawn out, as we shall explain later.

key_terms.أَوْصَافِ الْمَاءِ: the observable qualities of the water, such as color, taste, or smell
key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: a child whose urination is mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well under discussion as a source of water
key_terms.بَوْلٌ: urine as a contaminant affecting ritual purity
key_terms.تَغَيَّرَ: changed, meaning the water’s properties were altered by contamination
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: wine, an impure substance mentioned with the same ruling context
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: is to be drawn out or removed from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if urine or wine falls into a well in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage addresses the ruling of a well contaminated by urine or wine and states that all of its water is drawn out when the water’s characteristics have changed. It also clarifies that if no change occurs in the water, then a specified lesser amount is to be drawn, indicating a more detailed fiqh distinction in ritual purity rulings.
